title: External product compares the supported localization triangles
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ has characteristic $p$, $\ell\ne p$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, $n\ge1$, and $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. All schemes below are separated and of finite type over $k$. Work on their small pro-etale sites with bounded constructible constant-$A$ module complexes of finite Tor amplitude, denoted $D^b_{ctf}(-,A)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Use the geometric operations and specified constructible exceptional adjunctions of [def-trf-admissibility], and the external tensor product and canonical comparisons of [def-sf-kv-maps] specialized to $A$.

Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow Y$ be a closed immersion, $j:V\hookrightarrow Y$ its complementary open immersion, $T$ another such scheme, $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ and $Q\in D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$. Put $I=i\times\operatorname{id}_T$, $J=j\times\operatorname{id}_T$, $K=L\boxtimes Q$. Write $\mathcal T_Y(L)$ and $\mathcal T_{Y\times T}(K)$ for the supported distinguished triangles of [prop-sf-localization-all-stages](3), with their specified exceptional counit, ordinary open unit and connecting map. Write
$$c_i:(i_*i^!L)\boxtimes Q\xrightarrow{\sim}I_*(i^!L\boxtimes Q),\qquad c_j:(Rj_*j^*L)\boxtimes Q\xrightarrow{\sim}RJ_*(j^*L\boxtimes Q)$$
for the canonical ordinary product isomorphisms of [lem-trf-ordinary-kunneth], identifying $j^*L\boxtimes Q=J^*K$ by the pullback-composition and tensor comparisons. Then
$$\bigl(I_*\alpha_{i,\operatorname{id}_T}(L,Q)\circ c_i,\ \operatorname{id}_K,\ c_j\bigr)$$
is a morphism of distinguished triangles from $\mathcal T_Y(L)\boxtimes Q$ to $\mathcal T_{Y\times T}(K)$. In particular, all three squares, including the connecting square with the shift of its first component, commute. The assertion identifies the specified first component; it does not assume that the exceptional product comparison is invertible.

proof.text: The projection $Y\times_kT\to Y$ identifies $I,J$ with the base changes of $i,j$. The closed- and open-immersion base-change lemmas therefore apply. Their images are the inverse images of the complementary subsets $|Z|,|V|$, so they are complementary. The schemes $Y\times T,Z\times T,V\times T$ are separated finite type over $k$: finite affine covers of the factors give finite covers by $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_k C)$, whose coordinate algebras are generated by the union of finite sets of algebra generators; the diagonal of each product is the product of the two closed diagonals, hence is closed by the closed-immersion product lemma. This checks the geometric hypotheses for localization on the product.

source.place: Paragraph 2, closed immersions by localization: geometry of the product immersion pair

proof.text: Put $F(M)=M\boxtimes Q=Lp_Y^*M\otimes_A^L Lp_T^*Q$. Derived pullback is triangulated by the definition of the finite pro-etale operations, and derived tensor is exact in each variable by the ringed-projection exactness lemma. Thus $F$ is exact with the composite of their canonical shift comparisons. Apply localization (3), (1')--(3') to $L$ and to $K=F(L)$. It gives the specified distinguished triangles, and applying $F$ to the first gives a distinguished triangle whose connecting arrow is $F$ of the specified connecting arrow followed by $F(M[1])\cong F(M)[1]$. Stability (i),(ii) puts $K$ and the external products of all vertices in $D^b_{ctf}$. We use this category as a full triangulated subcategory, as asserted by the finite-ctf triangulated lemma.

source.place: Paragraph 2 and retained parent Step 6: external-tensor image of the supported triangle

proof.text: Apply ordinary Kunneth to $(f,M)=(i,Ri^!L)$ and $(j,j^*L)$, with auxiliary scheme $T$ and coefficient $Q$. The inputs are finite-Tor constructible by localization (2'),(3'), so its two isomorphisms are precisely $c_i,c_j$. Pullback composition and the monoidal pullback comparison give $J^*K\cong j^*L\boxtimes Q$; the same comparisons identify the pullbacks used below. Write $H=Ri^!L\boxtimes Q$, $D=j^*L\boxtimes Q=J^*K$, $A_0=(i_*Ri^!L)\boxtimes Q$ and $C_0=(Rj_*j^*L)\boxtimes Q$. Thus $c_i:A_0\cong I_*H$ and $c_j:C_0\cong RJ_*D$.

source.place: Paragraph 2 and retained parent Step 6: the two ordinary product identifications

proof.text:
We compute the ordinary transpose of these specified comparisons from definitions, rather than from the proof of ordinary Kunneth. For $f=i$ or $j$, put $h=f\times\operatorname{id}_T$, let $r:X\times T\to X$, $s:Y\times T\to Y$, and let $t,t'$ be the projections to $T$. Denote ordinary counits by $e$. The canonical comparison is $c_f=\pi_{h;r^*M,t'^*Q}\circ(\operatorname{Ex}_{*,f,M}\otimes1)$, with the composition identifications suppressed. Both factors have the explicit definitions in def-exchange-projection. Substituting the projection-map transpose and using naturality of $e_h$ gives
$$e_h\circ h^*c_f=(e_{h,r^*M}\circ h^*\operatorname{Ex}_{*,f,M})\otimes1_{t^*Q}.$$
The exchange-map transpose in that definition is exactly $r^*e_{f,M}$. Consequently
$$e_h\circ h^*c_f=r^*e_{f,M}\otimes1_{t^*Q}.$$
These equalities use the monoidal pullback comparison; cancellation of the unit in the displayed mate formulas is the adjunct-counit identity.

source.place: Paragraph 2, canonical open-product comparison: explicit expansion of its ordinary transpose

proof.text: Normalize the closed exceptional counits before using $\alpha$. For $a=i,I$, localization (2) identifies its right adjoint with the specified exceptional inverse image. The left adjoint $Ra_!$ identifies with $Ra_*$ using the proper compactification $(\operatorname{id},a)$: closed immersions are proper, and this is exactly the normalization in the geometric operation datum. Transport the right adjoint by the conjugate of this left-adjoint identification. It is an isomorphism by the adjunction-conjugate bijection. Expanding that conjugate and cancelling the adjacent unit/counit by the triangle identity gives $\varepsilon^{\mathrm{loc}}_a=\varepsilon^{\mathrm{adm}}_a\circ Ra_!(\sigma_a)$ under the left identification, where $\sigma_a$ is the conjugate right-adjoint comparison. Hence, after this adjunction-compatible identification, the localization counit is the admissibility counit, not an arbitrarily chosen counit on isomorphic functors. For $\operatorname{id}_T$, the same conjugate to the identity adjunction identifies $R\operatorname{id}_!$, $R\operatorname{id}^!$ with the identity and its counit with $1_Q$. These are the identifications in the following calculation.

source.place: Paragraph 2 and retained parent Step 6: identify the two specified exceptional adjunctions

proof.text:
We now compute $\mathrm{Ku}_!$ from def-sf-kv-maps(i) with $f_1=i,f_2=\operatorname{id}_T$, $B_1=Ri^!L,B_2=Q$. In its notation the base is $Y\times T$, $u=I$, $v=\operatorname{id}_{Y\times T}$ and $W=Z\times T$. Put $B=pr_Z^*Ri^!L$, $N=pr_T^*Q$. The relative identity-factor formula of lem-sf-kunneth-coherence(iv) gives $\kappa_{I,\operatorname{id}}(B,N)=\operatorname{PF}_{I,B,N}^{-1}$. The second exchange in def-sf-kv-maps(i) is the identity, since it is exchange for an identity vertical map; substitution in the exchange definition cancels its identity-adjunction unit and counit. Thus the defining composite is
$$\mathrm{Ku}_!=(\operatorname{Ex}_{!,1}^{-1}\otimes1_N)\circ\operatorname{PF}_{I,B,N}^{-1}.$$
Use the proper compactifications $(\operatorname{id},i)$ and $(\operatorname{id},I)$ from Step 5. In def-exchange-projection the open base-change and open projection factors are then identities, so $\operatorname{Ex}_{!,1}=\operatorname{Ex}_{*,1}$ and $\operatorname{PF}_{I,B,N}=\pi_{I;B,N}$. Consequently
$$\mathrm{Ku}_!^{-1}=\pi_{I;B,N}\circ(\operatorname{Ex}_{*,1}\otimes1_N)=c_i.$$
The last equality is exactly the canonical comparison formula of Step 4. Hence $\mathrm{Ku}_!\circ c_i=1_{A_0}$. All inputs to the relative formula are finite-Tor constructible by stability (i),(ii).

source.place: Paragraph 2 and retained parent Step 6: ordinary versus compact-support product normalization

proof.text:
Write $\varepsilon$ for the exceptional counits identified in Step 5. Definition def-sf-kv-maps(ii) and the adjunct-counit identity give
$$\varepsilon_I\circ I_*\alpha_{i,\operatorname{id}_T}(L,Q)=(\varepsilon_i\boxtimes1_Q)\circ\mathrm{Ku}_!.$$
Precompose with $c_i$ and use Step 6. The result is
$$\varepsilon_I\circ I_*\alpha_{i,\operatorname{id}_T}(L,Q)\circ c_i=\varepsilon_i\boxtimes1_Q.$$
Thus $a=I_*\alpha_{i,\operatorname{id}_T}(L,Q)\circ c_i$ and $b=1_K$ commute with the first arrows of the two triangles.

source.place: Paragraph 2 and retained parent Step 6: the specified first square

proof.text:
Let $\eta_j:L\to Rj_*j^*L$ and $\eta_J:K\to RJ_*J^*K$ be the ordinary units specified in localization (3), and denote their ordinary counits by $e_j,e_J$. Under $J^*K=D$, the $J^*\dashv RJ_*$ transpose of $c_j\circ(\eta_j\boxtimes1)$ is, by Step 4 and pullback naturality,
$$(e_j\boxtimes1)\circ(j^*\eta_j\boxtimes1)=(e_j\circ j^*\eta_j)\boxtimes1=1_D.$$
The equality in the middle is the ordinary adjunction triangle identity. The transpose of $\eta_J$ is also $1_D$. The ordinary Hom bijection is injective, so $c_j\circ(\eta_j\boxtimes1)=\eta_J$. This proves the second square for the specified $c_j$; naturality alone would not suffice.

source.place: Paragraph 2 and retained parent Step 6: open-unit square by transposition

proof.text:
The required orthogonality concerns the source vertex $A_0$, not the first vertex of the target triangle. By Step 3, $A_0\cong I_*H$ with $H=Ri^!L\boxtimes Q\in D^b_{ctf}(Z\times T,A)$. Localization (2) supplies $I_*\dashv RI^!$, and clause (4') on $Y\times T$ gives $RI^!RJ_*D=0$. Since shifts preserve the finite-Tor constructible category, for every integer $m$ the adjunction gives
$$\operatorname{Hom}(I_*(H[m]),RJ_*D)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(H[m],RI^!RJ_*D)=0.$$
The derived direct image commutes with shifts by its triangulated construction. Transporting along $c_i[m]$ therefore yields $\operatorname{Hom}(A_0[m],RJ_*D)=0$, in particular for $m=1$. This uses vanishing for arbitrary closed-source objects via adjunction, rather than the narrower same-object Hom formula of localization (3).

source.place: Retained parent Step 6: orthogonality with the actual external-tensor source vertex

proof.text: TR3 applied to the first square of Step 7 gives $c':C_0\to RJ_*D$ completing $(a,1_K)$ to a morphism of the two distinguished triangles, including the connecting square. Both $c'$ and $c_j$ satisfy the second square by Step 8, so $d=c'-c_j$ satisfies $d\circ(\eta_j\boxtimes1)=0$. Apply clause (ii) of Hom-out-of-triangle exactness to the source triangle $A_0\to K\to C_0\xrightarrow{w}A_0[1]$, with target $RJ_*D$. It gives $u:A_0[1]\to RJ_*D$ such that $d=u\circ w$. Step 9 makes $u=0$, hence $c'=c_j$. Substituting into the TR3 connecting equation gives $a[1]\circ w=w'\circ c_j$. Together with Steps 7 and 8 this proves exactly the displayed morphism of triangles, with the canonical external-product shift comparison of Step 2.
